high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Approves Bank's Capital Increase to Nearly 77.8 Trillion VND
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam has approved BIDV's request to increase charter capital by up to 4.982 trillion VND from retained earnings reserves, raising total charter capital from 72.8 trillion VND to 77.782 trillion VND. This follows a previous capital increase in March from 70.214 trillion to 72.8 trillion VND through private placement. BIDV's shareholders also approved a comprehensive capital increase plan of up to 26.757 trillion VND through three components: stock issuance from reserves (498 million shares at 6.8477% ratio), dividend payments in shares (up to 21.759 trillion VND), and private placement to strategic investors (up to 500 million shares). This massive recapitalization strengthens BIDV's financial position and supports lending capacity, which is crucial for Vietnam's banking sector stability and credit growth targets.

high.title: Banks Building Capital Flows for Mega-Cities
high.summary: SBV's Regional Branch 2 reported outstanding credit in Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai reached over 6.03 million billion VND by end-April 2026, up 3.84% from year-end 2025, accounting for 31.1% of national credit. Credit flows concentrated in productive sectors: manufacturing up 5.8%, agriculture up 5.4%, wholesale/retail up 4.4%, construction up 3.3%, and transport up 3.1%. This demonstrates credit alignment with real economic growth drivers rather than speculative activities. For FX traders, this controlled credit expansion supports sustainable economic growth without creating excessive liquidity that could pressure the VND. The focus on productive sectors rather than real estate or consumption suggests disciplined monetary policy that should help maintain exchange rate stability.

high.title: Stock Market Liquidity "Vanishes" Ahead of World Cup
high.summary: Vietnam stock market hit 14-month low liquidity with HOSE trading value plunging 49% to 10.133 trillion VND, with matched orders dropping to just 9.3 trillion VND. This marks the lowest liquidity since the historic surge following tariff storms in April 2025. June 2026 average daily matched trading reached only 13,000 trillion VND/session, down 37% from May. This represents the lowest monthly average liquidity since January 2025. The dramatic liquidity drought suggests investor risk-off sentiment and potential capital outflows from Vietnamese equities. For bond investors, this could indicate flight-to-safety dynamics that might benefit government bonds. The timing ahead of World Cup suggests seasonal factors, but the magnitude indicates deeper market concerns about economic outlook or external pressures.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Bar Prices Evening 10/6 Continue to Decline
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued steep decline with SJC gold quoted at 133.2-138.2 million VND/tael, down 5.4 million VND/tael. This represents one of the sharpest declines in recent weeks, bringing gold to lowest levels since early February 2026, creating significant losses for investors who bought at peak prices.

medium.title: State Bank of Vietnam Notes for Public When Buying Gold
medium.summary: SBV issued guidance on gold purchasing as the agency managing state gold trading activities. The regulatory framework has been continuously improved through Decree 24/2012 and amendments in Decree 232/2025, aimed at strengthening gold market management and reducing "goldization" in the economy. This regulatory clarity supports currency stability objectives.

medium.title: Savings Interest Rates on 10/6 at Major Banks
medium.summary: 12-month deposit rates range from 3.7% to 7% annually across 34 banks. Big4 state banks maintain uniform rates: 1-3 months at 4.75%, 6-9 months at 6.6%, 12-18 months at 6.8%. The convergence of state bank rates with commercial banks suggests coordinated monetary policy stance, supporting overall financial stability and VND stability.

medium.title: Expert: Declining Gold Prices Lead to More Selling Than Buying, Supporting Exchange Rate
medium.summary: Expert Nguyen Xuan Thanh noted that falling gold prices are causing more public selling than buying, which helps support the VND/USD exchange rate. He highlighted external shocks affecting major economies' interest rate adjustment paths, particularly the US, while US economy shows resilience with strong employment data and stable inflation around 4.3%.

medium.title: Au Lac Group Increases ACB Ownership Above 8%
medium.summary: Nguyen Duc Hieu Johnny increased ACB holdings by 1.95 million shares on June 5, raising personal stake to 1.90%. Including related persons, the group now holds over 8.02% of ACB shares, demonstrating continued confidence in the bank's prospects despite market volatility.
